Explanation: A wholesale used vehicle, represented by a listing with condition, title, pricing and inspection data, is the Core Value Unit exchanged through the ACV marketplace inside the proposed combined architecture.

This is a proposed post-close Owner view, not a claim that the acquisition has already closed. Copart would own ACV, while ACV is expected to continue as an independent subsidiary led by its existing management.
The strategic job is to own and grow an adjacent dealer-to-dealer network without rebuilding both marketplace sides from zero.
The opportunity is to broaden Copart's vehicle mix and use complementary demand, supply, infrastructure and data to increase liquidity and commercial reach.
Owning both marketplaces does not guarantee that the networks reinforce one another. Integration, participant fit and cross-side activation have to create real additional value.
ACV matches wholesale supply and demand and earns auction and related service fees when transactions occur.
Transaction Flows: ← Provider · Listing — Selling dealers and commercial consignors place wholesale vehicles and associated vehicle information into the ACV marketplace. | ← Consumer · Bid / Pay — Buying dealers bid or purchase through the marketplace and send payment into the transaction process. | → Consumer · Match — The marketplace gives buyers matched access to relevant wholesale inventory, condition information and auction execution. | → Provider · Payout — After a successful transaction, the marketplace completes settlement and value flows back to the selling side.

Explanation: The Owner layer governs participation, auction rules, condition information, arbitration, data use and the boundaries between the two marketplaces.
Dealer relationships, account management and the digital marketplace drive acquisition and repeat participation; Copart adds additional global buyer reach and commercial relationships.
ACV inspects vehicles and runs the digital auction and transaction journey, while Copart can add physical infrastructure, buyer reach and commercial distribution after closing.
The proposed combination joins ACV's dealer relationships, marketplace data and inspection technology with Copart's approximately one million members and more than 250 physical locations.

Independent and franchise dealers buy wholesale vehicles to replenish inventory. In the proposed combined architecture, this existing ACV demand could also be complemented by selected buyers from Copart's much larger global buyer network.
Buyers need to source the right used vehicles for inventory at workable economics.
They gain broad inventory access together with condition information, marketplace history and digital transaction tools that reduce uncertainty.
The buyer has to find suitable inventory while judging condition, price, title and resale risk without physically inspecting every vehicle.
Buying dealers bid or purchase through the marketplace and pay for successful transactions.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Bid / Pay — Buying dealers bid or purchase through the marketplace and send payment into the transaction process. | ← Owner · Match — The marketplace gives buyers matched access to relevant wholesale inventory, condition information and auction execution. | ← Partner · Delivery — The transportation partner physically delivers the purchased vehicle to the buyer or destination.

Explanation: The marketplace is primarily B2B; dealer and commercial participants must meet ACV's eligibility and account requirements.
ACV's auctions are accessible through mobile apps, desktop and API integrations.
Buyers repeatedly search inventory, compare vehicles, bid and purchase.
They contribute purchasing capacity plus demand signals, bidding behavior and inventory preferences that improve marketplace matching and data depth.
Dealers and commercial consignors supply wholesale vehicles. The strategic value of ACV to Copart is that this seller network already exists rather than having to be recruited from scratch.
Sellers need to move used vehicles efficiently into wholesale demand.
They seek faster inventory turn, broad bidder reach and competitive sale outcomes.
Slow disposition ties up capital and space, while disputes over condition or disclosures can reduce confidence and economics.
Sellers place wholesale vehicles into the marketplace and complete a sale when buyer demand clears.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Listing — Selling dealers and commercial consignors place wholesale vehicles and associated vehicle information into the ACV marketplace. | ← Owner · Payout — After a successful transaction, the marketplace completes settlement and value flows back to the selling side. | → Partner · Vehicle — When integrated transportation is used, the sold vehicle enters ACV's third-party carrier network for physical movement.

Explanation: Dealer and commercial sellers must satisfy ACV's marketplace participation and account requirements.
Sellers launch inventory through ACV's digital interfaces, integrations and operational channels.
They repeatedly list vehicles, provide vehicle information and manage reserve or pricing decisions.
They contribute the vehicle supply and the title, condition and inventory data required to transact.

Third-party transportation carriers are the clearest external Partner role in ACV's digital wholesale model. ACV integrates their capacity into checkout so vehicles can move from selling locations to buyers nationwide.
Carriers physically move purchased vehicles between sellers, ACV-related locations and buyers.
Integrated marketplace demand can provide recurring transport volume and route opportunities.
Transport economics depend on utilization, routing, distance and reliable pickup and delivery coordination.
Carriers receive vehicles into the transport network and deliver them to the buying side.
Transaction Flows: ← Provider · Vehicle — When integrated transportation is used, the sold vehicle enters ACV's third-party carrier network for physical movement. | → Consumer · Delivery — The transportation partner physically delivers the purchased vehicle to the buyer or destination.

Explanation: Transportation capacity is provided through ACV's network of third-party carrier partners rather than by any carrier automatically participating.
Carrier capacity is orchestrated through ACV Transportation and its technology-supported transport network.
Carriers pick up, move, deliver and provide status information for vehicle shipments.
They contribute transport assets, driver capacity and geographic coverage that let a digital transaction end in physical delivery.
